statement: The function returns a result r. Call a start index s admissible when 0 ≤ s ≤ len(nums)-k and the k entries nums[s], nums[s+1], ..., nums[s+k-1] are pairwise distinct (for all i,j with s ≤ i < j < s+k, nums[i] ≠ nums[j]). For an admissible s let sum(s) = Σ_{t=0}^{k-1} nums[s+t]. If at least one admissible s exists, then r = sum(s*) for some admissible s* and sum(s) ≤ r for every admissible s. If no admissible s exists, then r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: For every nums and k satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≥ 0.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = 0 or r ≥ k, with k viewed as a natural number.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≤ 100000 * k, with k viewed as a natural number.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let W = max{Σ_{t=0}^{k-1} nums[s+t] | 0 ≤ s ≤ len(nums)-k}; then r ≤ W.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every admissible start index s (that is, 0 ≤ s ≤ len(nums)-k and nums[s], ..., nums[s+k-1] are pairwise distinct), we have Σ_{t=0}^{k-1} nums[s+t] ≤ r.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if at least one admissible start index exists (that is, some s with 0 ≤ s ≤ len(nums)-k and nums[s], ..., nums[s+k-1] pairwise distinct), then there exists such an admissible start index s with r = Σ_{t=0}^{k-1} nums[s+t].
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no start index s with 0 ≤ s ≤ len(nums)-k such that nums[s], ..., nums[s+k-1] are pairwise distinct.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: For every integer c and every array nums' of the same length as nums such that nums'[i] = nums[i] + c for all i and nums' also satisfies the same bounds with the same k (in particular len(nums') ≤ 100000 and 1 ≤ nums'[i] ≤ 100000), whenever the function returns r on (nums,k) and returns r' on (nums',k): a start index s is admissible for nums exactly when it is admissible for nums' (where admissible means 0 ≤ s ≤ len-k and the length-k block is pairwise distinct); if no admissible start exists then r = r' = 0; if at least one admissible start exists then r' = r + k*c.
preconditions: len(nums) ≥ 1; len(nums) ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums); for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.
